overview.title: Contents (end): chapters 19-20 and index
overview.main_topic: The last contents page: sections 19.3-19.4 on how to build intelligence, chapter 20 (conclusions) and the index.
overview.central_idea: The book ends with the authors' proposal for how intelligence might be built (abstraction, on-the-fly adaptation, the ARC benchmarks, combining deep learning with program synthesis) and a concluding review of key concepts, limitations, outlook and how to keep learning.
overview.importance: It shows where the book's big-picture argument and its recap of all key concepts live — useful both as a preview and as a revision guide.
learning_objectives: Locate the discussion of the kaleidoscope hypothesis, ARC Prize and ARC-AGI 2.
Find the program-synthesis and 'search and symbols' material in 19.4.
Use chapter 20.1 as a revision map of the whole book.

paragraphs.excerpt: The kaleidoscope hypothesis 577 ■ The essence of intelligence: Abstraction acquisition and
paragraphs.what_it_says: Section 19.3 'How to build intelligence' lists the kaleidoscope hypothesis (577), abstraction acquisition and recombination as the essence of intelligence (578), setting the right target (578), on-the-fly adaptation as a new target (580), the ARC Prize (581), the test-time adaptation era (582) and ARC-AGI 2 (583).
paragraphs.what_it_means: The authors define intelligence in terms of abstraction and adaptation to new situations, and discuss benchmarks designed to measure that (ARC).
paragraphs.why_it_matters: This frames what 'progress toward AGI' should be measured against, according to the book.

terminology.meaning: the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus, a benchmark of novel reasoning puzzles (ARC-AGI)
adapting a model to each new task at inference time

paragraphs.excerpt: The two poles of abstraction 585 ■ Cognition as a combination of
paragraphs.what_it_says: Section 19.4 'The missing ingredients: Search and symbols' lists the two poles of abstraction (585), cognition as a combination of both (587), why deep learning isn't a complete answer to abstraction generation (588), program synthesis (589), blending deep learning and program synthesis (590), modular recombination and lifelong learning (592) and the long-term vision (593).
paragraphs.what_it_means: The authors argue that deep learning covers one kind of abstraction and that search-based program synthesis is needed for the other; combining both is their proposed direction.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: It is the book's most forward-looking claim and clearly labelled as such by the headings.

continually accumulating and reusing learned components over time

paragraphs.excerpt: Various approaches to artificial intelligence 596 ■ What makes deep learning special
paragraphs.what_it_says: Section 20.1 'Key concepts in review' lists various approaches to AI (596), what makes deep learning special within ML (596), how to think about deep learning (597), key enabling technologies (598), the universal ML workflow (599), and key network architectures (600).
paragraphs.what_it_means: A recap of the whole book's main ideas in one place.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Ideal for revision: each subsection points back to material covered across chapters 1-18.
connections: p.620: approaches to AI and what makes DL special (printed 596)
p.623: the universal ML workflow, recapping chapter 6 (printed 599)

paragraphs.excerpt: Practice on real-world problems using Kaggle 607 ■ Read about the latest
paragraphs.what_it_says: Under 20.4 'Staying up to date in a fast-moving field' the subsections are practice on real-world problems using Kaggle (607), reading about the latest developments on arXiv (607), and exploring the Keras ecosystem (608).
paragraphs.what_it_means: Concrete advice for continuing to learn after the book: competitions, preprints and the Keras ecosystem.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Deep learning changes fast, so the book ends with ways to keep current.

deeper.title: Using printed vs. PDF page numbers
deeper.body: The numbers in this table of contents are the book's printed page numbers. This companion links by PDF page number. For the main body of the book, **PDF page = printed page + 24** (for example, chapter 20 starts on printed page 595, which is PDF p.619). The offset was checked against the chapter-opener pages; it is a property of this PDF, not something the book states.

misconceptions.claim: The page numbers in the contents are the PDF page numbers.
misconceptions.correction: They are printed page numbers. In this PDF the main body is offset by 24 pages (e.g. printed 16 = PDF p.40).

misconceptions.claim: Sections 19.3-19.4 present settled facts about how to build AGI.
misconceptions.correction: The headings show these sections present the authors' hypotheses and proposals (e.g. the kaleidoscope hypothesis, blending deep learning with program synthesis); they should be read as argued positions.

later.note: 19.4 the missing ingredients: search and symbols.

takeaways: 19.3-19.4 present the authors' view: intelligence as abstraction and on-the-fly adaptation, measured by ARC, with program synthesis as a missing ingredient.
20.1 is a one-stop review of the book's key concepts and architectures.
The book ends with practical ways to stay current: Kaggle, arXiv and the Keras ecosystem.
